messages:
incident-bot: [PAGER] smart-routing: fallback-loop detected for /api/generate — error rate ↑4x, retries spiking, region fallback chatter. Affected cluster: prod-eu/us-west-2. Dashboard: https://console.redwood.ai/d/alerts/routing-fallback

alice (oncall): ack. paging bob and carol. I'm on it.

bob (sre): looking — seeing continuous 'route->region B -> route->region A' on the routing graph, TTL on policy keys is 0. Also seeing model mismatch logs: 'variant not compatible' on some fallbacks.

carol (platform): @alice @bob FYI I just got a deploy hook from deploy-bot: routing-policy v2.3.4 applied 3h ago (deploy-bot reported success). Could be a bad policy change.

deploy-bot: deploy: routing-policy v2.3.4 applied to `prod` (hash: a1b2c3). CI: green.

alice (oncall): customers complaining on support channel. Elaine, can you surface an impact summary?

elaine (support): affected customers ~12 orgs, top impacted: payments-service (5 regions), churn-risk: 2 larger customers seeing 500s. Posting interim banner: "Intermittent generation errors — working on a mitigation" :warning:

dan (eng): quick read of logs — fallback policy references model aliases wrong: alias `xlnet-3b` maps to `xlnet-3b-quant` in eu, but to `xlnet-3b-fp16` in us. On fallback, runtime rejects tokenization mismatch causing 500s.

bob (sre): that explains the 'variant not compatible' entries. We need to stop the loop — options: fix policy or force-route traffic to a single stable region/model. I can patch policy but might take 10-15m to propagate. Manual override faster.

carol (platform): I'm going to perform a forced traffic shift to a single region and pin model variant to stable while we fix mapping. Will annotate and monitor.

carol (platform): `rwctl route override --service api/generate --region us-east-1 --model xlnet-3b-stable --duration 30m --reason "mitigate fallback loop" --author carol`

alice (oncall): approved. @bob monitor latency/queue depth after shift. Elaine keep customers updated.

bob (sre): override applied. immediate drop in 500s from EU customers, error-rate down to ~0.5x baseline. p95 latency rose from 220ms -> 980ms on pinned region. GPU queue depth on us-east-1 nodes now at 95%.

elaine (support): customers reporting fewer 500s, but some report timeouts. Posting update to support thread.

dan (eng): concern: forcing to us-east-1 moves stateful sessions for some customers (auth/timezone/regional keys). Seeing auth errors for region-bound tokens: `ERR_REGIONAL_TOKEN_MISMATCH`.

bob (sre): yep, SES logs show ~1200 token mismatch errors since override. Looks like session affinity wasn't respected.

carol (platform): unexpected. I didn't expect regional session affinity to fail at scale. Looks like a dependency on region metadata in the gateway that didn't follow the override path. Rolling back manual override to re-enable affinity while we push a safer config.

carol (platform): `rwctl route override --service api/generate --clear-override --author carol --note "rollback: affinity issues"`

carol (platform): rollback applied. traffic flows returned to distributed routing. 500s ticked back up in EU to previous levels within 2m.

alice (oncall): summary so far: manual override stopped fallback loop but caused high latency + auth/affinity failures for some customers. rollback reintroduced fallback-loop symptoms. Need a safer path.

dan (eng): immediate mitigation plan: 1) add a temporary compatibility shim on runtime to accept tokenization mapping across variants (10–20m), 2) revert mapping in routing policy to the pre-v2.3.4 alias table (if safe), 3) add circuit-breaker on fallback loop to prevent circular fallbacks.

bob (sre): implementing circuit-breaker in routing layer now: set `fallback_depth=1` and `disable-circular-fallback=true` in dynamic config. Patch rolling via `cfgctl apply routing.fallback` (ETA 6m).

carol (platform): I'm not going to use manual force-region again without confirming affinity and gateway invariants. Add a guard: `override_requires_affinity_check=true`.

elaine (support): updated customers: mitigation in progress, some short-term timeouts but overall fewer 500s. We'll send a follow-up once we have final root-cause.

bob (sre): circuit-breaker applied. early telemetry: fallback chatter dropped by 90%, error-rate trending down. p95 latency still elevated in some paths, but stable.

dan (eng): compatibility shim deployed to runtime canary (1 host). Testing with vendor tokenization cross-check — looks good. Planning broader rollout in 12m after smoke tests.

alice (oncall): great. can we capture exact impact numbers for postmortem? Elaine please pull number of affected requests, unique customers, and top error messages.

elaine (support): on it. ETA 30m for formal impact table.

carol (platform): next steps (short): 1) revert v2.3.4 alias change or update alias mapping to be explicit, 2) add routing guard rails for manual overrides (affinity check + preflight), 3) add an automated detection rule for circular fallback to page before it hits customer-facing errors, 4) update runbook to explicitly warn about force-region side-effects.

alice (oncall): agreed. I'll own the runbook updates. Bob/Dan/Carol — create follow-up tasks and PRs. Postmortem schedule: tomorrow 11:00.

carol (platform): added follow-up tasks: DOCS-123 (runbook), PLAT-456 (override guard rails), RTE-789 (alias mapping revert).

deploy-bot: recovery: routing.fallback circuit-breaker applied; runtime shim canary deployed to 1/8 canary hosts.

alice (oncall): thanks team. marking this thread resolved for now but leaving incident open till canary -> prod rollout completes and impact table published.

incident-bot: incident state: mitigated (partial) — severity lowered to S2. Next update expected in 30m.
